fields.label: Sample type
fields.help: treated = nuclease + donor · no donor = nuclease only · mock = neither

fields.label: Nuclease
fields.help: Recorded for your records only. The nuclease the analysis uses is set in Experiment design.

fields.label: Genome region (hg38)
fields.note: The stretch of chromosome your amplicon sits in. Click Fetch reference window if it is not downloaded yet.
fields.more: Written as chromosome:start..end:strand and fetched from Ensembl. Changing it re-derives the cached FASTA name and the start coordinate, so those two never drift from the region.

design.name: Nuclease and guide

fields.label: Nuclease
fields.note: Fills the two cut positions below. No tool reads this.

fields.label: Guide spacer (5'->3')
fields.note: The spacer sequence. The console finds it in the amplicon, on either strand, and marks the cut.

fields.label: Cut position, counted from the guide start
fields.note: How many bases from the guide's 5' end the cut falls. The Nuclease selector fills it.
fields.more: SpCas9 17, AsCas12a 18, ARCUS 11. It must always be exactly one more than the CRISPRLungo value below, which counts the same cut a different way; the Nuclease selector keeps the pair consistent for you.

fields.label: Same cut position, as CRISPRLungo counts it
fields.note: Always one less than the value above. The Nuclease selector fills it.
fields.more: CRISPRLungo takes a 0-based index into the guide for the last base before the cut, so it is always one less than the offset above. Verified against the tool's source: it is applied from the spacer's own 5' end and works on either strand.

design.note: Pick your nuclease and the two cut positions fill themselves in.

design.name: Primers
design.note: Your two primers, entered twice: once as the part that matches the genome, once as you ordered them.

fields.label: Forward primer (genome-matching part)
fields.note: The part of the primer that matches the genome, without any tail. Sets the amplicon's left end.

fields.label: Reverse primer (genome-matching part)
fields.note: The part that matches the genome. Sets the amplicon's right end.

fields.label: Forward primer as ordered
fields.note: Optional. Include the 5' tail if your primer has one.
fields.more: Only ALPINE uses this, to check that a read is a complete amplicon: it keeps a read if any 10 bp of the primer appears near the matching end. Leave both of these empty and that check is simply skipped, which is safe. Must be at least 10 bp.

fields.label: Reverse primer as ordered
fields.note: Optional. Enter it as ordered, not reverse-complemented.
fields.more: ALPINE reverse-complements it itself, so entering it already reverse-complemented would make every read fail. Fill both of these or neither.

design.more: The two entries do different jobs. The genome-matching part is used to find your amplicon in the reference genome, and it is required - a primer with a synthetic 5' tail would never be found there. The as-ordered version is what is physically on your reads, and it is passed to ALPINE as an optional check that a read is a complete amplicon. CRISPRLungo never uses a primer at all. If your primers have no tail, the two entries are simply the same sequence.

design.name: Donor
design.note: Where your knock-in sequence comes from. Pick one source - a FASTA file, or a row of a paper's table.

fields.label: Donor: knock-in allele (FASTA file)
fields.note: A FASTA of the edited allele with wild-type sequence on both sides.
fields.more: The homology arms and the inserted sequence are worked out from wherever this differs from the wild-type amplicon.

fields.label: Donor: supplementary table (xlsx file)
fields.note: A spreadsheet from the paper, with a sheet named 'Table S1'.
fields.more: The sheet must have Full Sequence, Left Homology Arm and Right Homology Arm rows.

fields.label: Which row of that table
fields.help: TRAC CD19-CAR HDR template for editing with AsCas12a
fields.note: The exact title of the donor row to use.

fields.label: Homology arm length to record (bp)
fields.note: How much wild-type sequence each side of the insert counts as a homology arm. Only used with a donor FASTA.

design.name: Public data (only if you use it)
design.note: Leave both empty when your reads are files on the cluster and your donor is a FASTA.

fields.label: BioProject
fields.note: Only needed if your samples are public SRA runs.

fields.label: Europe PMC id
fields.note: Only needed if your donor comes from a paper's supplementary table.

design.name: Read lengths and scoring
design.note: These have sensible defaults. The console suggests read lengths once it knows your amplicon.

fields.label: Shortest read to keep (bp)
fields.note: Shorter reads are dropped before analysis. Nothing is subsampled.

fields.label: Longest read to keep (bp)
fields.note: Removes concatemers and chimeras far longer than your amplicon.

fields.label: How much of the insert a read must cover
fields.note: 0.8 means a read needs at least 80% of the inserted sequence to count as a knock-in.
fields.more: The same threshold is given to both tools so their two percentages answer the same question.

fields.label: Scoring window around the cut (bp) - CRISPRLungo
fields.note: Edits further than this from the cut are not counted. Keep it equal to the ALPINE window below.
fields.more: A half-width, so 25 means 25 bp either side. It must cover every mutation you intended, including PAM-blocking changes that sit well away from the cut. It also bounds knock-in detection, so lowering it silently lowers the knock-in percentage.

fields.label: Scoring window around the cut (bp) - ALPINE
fields.note: The same idea for the other tool. Keep the two equal so both score the same span.
fields.more: ALPINE's own default is 20. At the exact edge of the window it counts a substitution but not an insertion, so matching it to the CRISPRLungo window removes a boundary case.

fields.label: Where ALPINE looks for the primer (bp from each read end)
fields.note: 150 here, rather than ALPINE's default of 50, because a nanopore read can carry leftover adapter and barcode before the primer.

fields.label: Sequencing platform
fields.note: Choosing nanopore also makes the pipeline switch ALPINE's hard-coded minimap2 preset to map-ont.

inputs.name: FASTQ (local)
inputs.format: gzipped FASTQ (`.fastq.gz`), one file per sample, absolute path on the cluster
inputs.use: The preferred source. Step `01_fetch` length-filters it with seqkit into `results/<analysis>/data/<sample_id>.fastq.gz`; the original file is never modified. Directories outside the repo are bound into the container automatically by the driver (`src/pipeline.py`).

inputs.name: SRA run accession
inputs.use: The alternative source, for public data. Step `01_fetch` checks the read count against ENA, downloads the `.sra` file, converts it with `fasterq-dump` and keeps it in the shared cache `data/raw/<run>.fastq.gz`, so later analyses reuse it.

inputs.name: sample_id
inputs.use: The row key. It names every file, log and SLURM job of the sample, so it must be unique within the sheet.

inputs.name: condition
inputs.use: A human-readable label for the treatment, e.g. `rnp_dsDNA_donor`. Carried into `summary.tsv` and the KI % matrix; not interpreted by the tools.

inputs.name: control
inputs.use: Marks a negative control. CRISPRLungo's `--control` is the first `mock` sample, else the first `no_donor` one (`src/analysis.py`, `control_sample`); at least one is required.

inputs.name: Wet-lab and sequencing fields
inputs.use: Provenance only. Stored in `configs/samples/<sample_id>.json` and copied into `results/<analysis>/meta/`; never read by the tools.

inputs.name: References (built by `02_refs`)
inputs.use: Control (unedited) and knock-in amplicons, the inserted gene, guide, primers and homology arms. Built from a genome window (`refs.region`) and the donor template table of the paper (`refs.pmc`). The files are named after the example locus (`TRAC`, `CAR`); their roles are the same for any target.

params.meaning: Minimum fraction of the inserted gene that a read must cover to be counted as a knock-in. 0.8 means at least 80% of the insert must be present; shorter, truncated integrations are not counted. The same threshold is applied to both tools so their percentages are comparable.
params.arg: ALPINE `truncated_cutoff` in job.yaml; for CRISPRLungo it is applied afterwards by `summarize.py` on the merged insert blocks

params.meaning: NCBI/ENA BioProject that the SRA runs belong to. Only used to download the run table from ENA, so that every downloaded run can be checked against its expected read count. Not needed when all samples are local FASTQ files.
Shortest read kept, in bp. Reads below this length are dropped before any tool sees them (primer dimers, broken reads). Nothing is subsampled: all passing reads are used.
Longest read kept, in bp. Removes concatemers and chimeric reads much longer than the knock-in amplicon.
hg38 genomic window (chromosome:start..end:strand) that contains the amplicon. Downloaded once from Ensembl and pinned by sha256.
Europe PMC id of the paper whose supplementary table holds the HDR donor templates. Downloaded once and pinned by sha256.
Local path of the cached hg38 window downloaded from `refs.region`.
1-based genomic coordinate of the first base of `genomic_fasta`; converts positions in the window back to hg38 coordinates.
Supplementary spreadsheet containing the donor templates (full sequence and homology arms).
Exact title of the row in the supplementary table to use as donor; selects the knock-in construct.

Nuclease used, chosen in the console's design panel. It fills cut_offset_from_guide_5p and lungo.cleavage_pos with the pair that matches it (AsCas12a 18/17, SpCas9 17/16, ARCUS 11/10) and is stored so the choice survives a reload. No tool reads it.
crRNA spacer sequence (5'->3'). Locates the cut site in the wild-type amplicon and is passed to CRISPRLungo.
Distance of the cut from the 5' end of the guide: 17 for SpCas9, 18 for AsCas12a. Wrong values shift the expected integration site.

The same two oligos as ordered, 5' adapter tail included, which is what is physically at the ends of every read. ALPINE is given these to recognise a complete amplicon within primer_check_length bases of each read end; the gene-specific part alone would sit a tail-length further in and complete reads would be rejected. When the primers carry no tail the two pairs are the same sequence.

The gene-specific part of each primer, without the adapter tail: the part that actually anneals to the genome. 02_refs searches the reference window for it and the two hits set the ends of the WT amplicon. The full oligo would never be found here, because its 5' tail is not genomic sequence.
Number of bases at each read end in which ALPINE looks for the primers. Reads whose primers are not found there are discarded as incomplete amplicons.
Read technology. `nanopore` tells ALPINE to expect ONT errors and also makes the pipeline patch ALPINE's hard-coded `minimap2 -ax map-hifi` into `map-ont`.
Position of the cut inside the guide as CRISPRLungo counts it; centres the window where edits are scored.
Half-width in bp around the cut in which CRISPRLungo scores indels and integrations. Larger values catch more distal edits but also more sequencing noise.
CPU, memory (MB) and time (minutes) of each job, set in `src/pipeline.py`. `get_best_node` uses them to choose a partition and node with enough free resources when each job is submitted.

Half-width in bp around the cut in which ALPINE scores indels and substitutions from the CIGAR. Upstream default 20; set to 25 here to match lungo.window so the two tools score the same span. ALPINE centres it on the midpoint of the WT row of config.tsv, which build_refs.py writes as the cut, so the two windows are concentric. Note the bound is inclusive for substitutions but strict for insertions.

commands.cmd: cwltool --no-container aav_per_sample_workflow.cwl job.yaml   # job.yaml: fastqfile, reffile, config, sample_name, primer_1, primer_2, primer_check_length, data_type, truncated_cutoff, five_prime_HA_seq, three_prime_HA_seq

python3 src/summarize.py --analysis-dir results/<analysis>
# summary.tsv: ki_reads/ki_pct, partial_reads/partial_pct (insert present but below the threshold), unclassified_reads (excluded from the denominator), notes = every outcome class with its %
